comparison: Both strongly support the asymmetric connectivity findings (C1, C2, C13-C17). OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation (p=0.0079, Fisher's exact test) and connection probabilities. Peer review affirms 'strength of evidence is solid' and praises the 'previously unappreciated structure.' Peer review also includes C37-C38 (predictions from connectivity) which OpenEval evaluates separately.

OpenEval supports the predictions/inferences (C37-C38) as logical extensions of connectivity data validated by behavioral experiments. Peer review includes these claims in their overall affirmation of the connectivity findings, treating them as part of the key contribution without separate evaluation.

Both support locomotion findings (C18-C20). OpenEval provides specific statistical details (DMS p=0.0046, DLS p=0.0003 for D1-SPN). Peer review groups locomotion with other behavioral data (C3, C21-C24) and affirms effects across 'three distinct behaviors' as strong convergent evidence.

Both support cortical stimulation locomotion effects (C21-C24). OpenEval details frequency-dependence and control experiments. Peer review combines these with other locomotion claims (C3, C18-C20) in affirming the behavioral verification of anatomical findings.

Both strongly support ICSS findings (C25-C28). OpenEval provides detailed permutation test results showing D1-projecting cortical neurons drive ICSS while noting both D1- and D2-projecting neurons support ICSS. Peer review includes C4 and affirms ICSS as part of 'three distinct behaviors' providing functional verification.

Both support sequence behavior findings (C31-C36). OpenEval details differential effects between MCC (D1 vs D2: p=0.0097) and M1 (no difference: p=0.4511). Peer review includes C5 and affirms sequence data as part of convergent behavioral evidence across three behaviors.

Both support the rabies-ChR2 methodology (C40-C43). OpenEval validates anatomical tracing and functional ChR2 expression with electrophysiological data. Peer review approves the methodological choice to patch mCherry-negative cells and notes editorial assessment deemed rabies tracing acceptable. Peer review also includes C59 (control experiments).

Both support control experiments validating specificity. OpenEval evaluates C57-C59 regarding cortical vs striatal stimulation controls, acknowledging limitations about collaterals. Peer review includes C59 with methodology approval but focuses more on rabies tracing validation than stimulation controls.

OpenEval rates mechanistic interpretations (C53-C55) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative inferences requiring targeted manipulations during specific sequence phases. Peer review rates these same claims as SUPPORTED, accepting the interpretive framework as valuable contribution to understanding corticostriatal function without expressing uncertainty.

OpenEval supports C39 (differential behavioral effects) as reasonable inference from behavioral data, noting it would benefit from direct cortical recordings. Peer review includes C39 with broader interpretive claims (C53-C55) and accepts the framework as adding to understanding of corticostriatal logic.

OpenEval rates C56 (prediction about cortical activity during behavior) as UNCERTAIN, noting it is untested speculation despite being reasonable. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific predictive claim.

OpenEval supports background claims C6-C12 as accurately representing established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not separately evaluate background/context claims.

OpenEval supports background claims C29-C30, C44-C51 as accurate literature representation providing context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these contextual claims.

OpenEval supports methodological documentation claims C60-C69 regarding statistical methods, connectivity criteria, and ethical procedures. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these methodological documentation claims.

Peer review includes C3 (general locomotion claim) grouped with specific locomotion findings. OpenEval does not have a separate result for C3; this claim may be implicitly covered in OpenEval R3 and R4 evaluations of specific locomotion experiments.

Peer review includes C4 (general ICSS claim) with specific ICSS findings. OpenEval does not have a separate result for C4; this claim may be implicitly covered in OpenEval R5 evaluation of specific ICSS experiments.

Peer review includes C5 (general sequence behavior claim) with specific sequence findings. OpenEval does not have a separate result for C5; this claim may be implicitly covered in OpenEval R6 evaluation of specific sequence behavior experiments.
